status.label: Fix plan ready for design
status.detail: A shell-peek visibility transition likely leaves Run state inconsistent.

next_action.label: Design fix
next_action.reason: Capture the Win+, event order and make hide idempotent.

judgment.rationale: The report includes a short deterministic sequence and video. Current Run UI relies on WPF deactivation/visibility transitions without an explicit shell desktop-peek path, making a visibility state race plausible and suitable for focused reproduction.
evidence: PowerToys 0.100.2 from the Store; open Run, press Win+,, observe a ghost window.
The reporter notes Command Palette closes correctly under the same shortcut.
PowerLauncher MainWindow handles Deactivated and IsVisibleChanged and hides through MainViewModel, but no Win+, shell-peek-specific handling was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce under Win+, trace activation/visibility events, then make shell peek collapse Run through the normal hide path.

fix_assessment.rationale: No merged fix was found; the current visibility state machine provides a focused hypothesis that requires message-order validation.

proposed_fixes.title: Collapse PowerToys Run when shell desktop peek deactivates it
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Win+, can temporarily move focus/desktop composition without producing the same activation sequence as an ordinary foreground-window change, allowing the WPF frame to remain visible after Run state has otherwise deactivated.
plan: Instrument the existing MainWindow Deactivated/IsVisibleChanged and MainViewModel.Hide transitions during Win+,.
Route the shell-peek/deactivation sequence through one idempotent hide operation that closes the Run surface and resets result/activation state.
Add an integration/UI regression test or extracted state-machine test for a visible launcher losing activation through desktop peek.
verification: Open Run, press and release Win+,, and verify no frame or hit-test surface remains.
Repeat with Win+D, Alt+Tab, Escape, and normal focus loss to ensure existing hide behavior remains.

confidence.rationale: The UI event surface is identified, but the exact Windows message/order produced by Win+, has not yet been captured.

issue_context.summary: While PowerToys Run is visible, invoking the Windows Win+, desktop-peek shortcut can leave a non-interactive Run frame visible instead of fully hiding the launcher.
known_information: The sequence is two steps and includes a recording.
The ghost occurs with PowerToys Run open and does not occur with Command Palette.
Run currently uses WPF visibility binding plus deactivation callbacks to hide.
inferences: Win+, likely follows a shell-specific activation/composition path that leaves visibility and launcher state out of sync.
issue_context.analysis: A current local reproduction can capture the exact WPF/window messages and turn the plausible visibility race into a narrow fix without requiring more reporter evidence.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live issue through 2026-08-26T09:24:41Z.
Reviewed PowerLauncher/MainWindow.xaml(.cs) and ViewModel/MainViewModel.cs visibility/deactivation handling at commit 33e4ef46e5db77a256818a917d65103c9b7398fa.
Searched upstream for another PowerToys Run ghost-window report tied to Win+, and found no duplicate.
